newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African platinum stocks jump with soaring metal.
newsitem.headline: S.African platinum stocks jump with soaring metal.

text.p: South African platinum shares leapt again on Friday morning, driven higher by a soaring metal price which hit its highest level since 1990.
At 0745 GMT the platinum index was up 2.7 percent at 5,124.0 with stocks showing gains across the board.

Impala Platinum Holdings Ltd gained 250 cents to 53.50 rand, Anglo American Platinum Corp Ltd gained 125 cents to 33.25, Rustenburg Platinum Holdings Ltd added 125 to 77.00 and marginal mine Northam Platinum Ltd was up 18 at 250.
Spot platinum surged $50 an ounce in early European trading to hit $480.00/$510.00 from Thursday's close of $430.00/$440.00.

Prices for platinum and its sister metal palladium have been soaring since the start of the year because of protracted delays in exports from major producer Russia and a build-up of speculative fund holdings of the metal.
Supply tightness and price volatility have become increasingly severe in recent days and market makers on Thursday held an emergency meeting to promote order in the market.
Palladium, which has been trading at the highest levels since 1980 this week, was bid at $235.00/$245.00 in early Europe.
